vinialesaurus:eswiki:4.title: Vinialesaurus (Rasgos que lo definen en una especie)

facts.statement: The species was first described in 1949 as a subspecies of Cryptocleidus by Ricardo De la Torre and Luis Rojas.
facts.quote: The combinatio nova of the type species is Vinialesaurus caroli, first described as the subspecies Cryptocleidus? cuervoi caroli by Ricardo De la Torre and Luis Rojas in 1949

facts.statement: The genus was redescribed and elevated to a distinct genus in 2002 by Zulma Gasparini, Bardet, and Iturralde.
facts.quote: redescribed by Zulma Gasparini, Bardet and Iturralde in 2002

facts.statement: The holotype fossil was prepared at the American Museum of Natural History between 1991 and 1992.
facts.quote: It was prepared in the American Museum of Natural History in 1991/1992

facts.statement: The genus name honors the town of Viñales in western Cuba where the fossils were found.
facts.quote: The name Vinialesaurus honors Viñales, the town in western Cuba where the fossil of Vinialesaurus was discovered

facts.statement: The species name honors the original discoverer, Carlos de la Torre y Huerta.
facts.quote: The specific name honours the discoverer, Carlos de la Torre y Huerta

facts.statement: This plesiosaur lived during the Late Jurassic (Oxfordian) in the Jagua Formation of Pinar del Río, Cuba.
facts.quote: Vinialesaurus is a genus of plesiosaur from the Late Jurassic (Oxfordian) Jagua Formation of Pinar del Río, Cuba

facts.statement: Taxonomically, Vinialesaurus belongs to the family Cryptoclididae.
facts.quote: but it was a cryptoclidid

facts.statement: The animal lived approximately 150 million years ago.
facts.quote: de hace unos 150 millones de años

facts.statement: Fossils of this genus have been found in the Caribbean and recently in South America.
facts.quote: Poblaron el Caribe y recientemente se ha descubierto que también Sudamérica

facts.statement: A second specimen was discovered in the Atacama Desert, specifically in Calama, Chile.
facts.quote: un segundo ejemplar en el Desierto de Atacama, más específicamente en Calama (Chile)

facts.statement: It possessed paddle-like flippers adapted for swimming in warm waters.
facts.quote: Posee patas transformadas en aletas que utilizaba para nadar en aguas cálidas

facts.statement: The animal had a long, thin neck ending in a relatively small head.
facts.quote: Su cuello era delgado y largo, terminado en una cabeza relativamente pequeña

facts.statement: It had serrated teeth, indicating it was a carnivore.
facts.quote: Tenía dientes aserrados lo que lo convertía en un carnívoro

facts.statement: Its body was rounded and it had a medium-length tail.
facts.quote: Su cuerpo era redondeado y su cola mediana

facts.statement: Estimates suggest the animal measured between four and ten meters in length and weighed between one and three tons.
facts.quote: Aunque resulta difícil decir su largo o peso medía entre cuatro y diez metros y pesaría entre una y tres toneladas

facts.statement: It lived in a diverse ecosystem located in the proto-Caribbean.
facts.quote: Este plesiosaurio vivió en un ecosistema muy amplio y variado localizado en el proto-Caribe

facts.statement: Placoderms, which were abundant in the Oxfordian, likely constituted part of its diet.
facts.quote: De los peces destacan los placodermos, muy abundantes en el Oxfordiano (Jurásico Tardío), y que podían constituir su alimento

facts.statement: It coexisted with the bivalve Trigonia krombelli, a genus that still exists in Australia.
facts.quote: También convivió con el bivalvo Trigonia krombelli, cuyo género aún habita en Australia

facts.statement: The Proto-Caribbean developed in a channel created between the continents of Laurasia and Gondwana.
facts.quote: Los continentes de Laurasia (al Norte) y Gondwana (al Sur) crearon un canal en el cual se desarrolló el Proto Caribe

facts.statement: Turtles such as Caribemys oxfordiensis likely nested in the same environment.
facts.quote: podían desovar tortugas como el Caribemys oxfordiensis

facts.statement: Other marine reptiles may have been the main competitors of Vinialesaurus.
facts.quote: Quizás los principales competidores del Vinialesaurus fueran otros reptiles marinos

facts.statement: The pliosaur Peloneustes was a predator with massive jaws nearly one meter long.
facts.quote: El Peloneustes era un depredador de inmensas mandíbulas de casi un metro de largo

facts.statement: Contradictions exist regarding pliosaurs and new species, though samples are constantly analyzed.
facts.quote: Acerca de los pliosaurios y nuevas especies existen contradicciones aunque se analizan constantemente muestras al igual que las de muchos otros de estos fascinantes animales

facts.statement: The time range for this genus is the Oxfordian stage, from 159 to 154.8 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Oxfordian to Oxfordian (159 to 154.8 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The holotype specimen includes the front skull, front lower jaws, and the first two vertebrae.
rejected.quote: The holotype consists of the front skull, front lower jaws, and the anterior two vertebrae (atlas and axis)
